speaker: Unknown
en: The thing about being a founder/CEO is there is no one there to rescue you.
zh: 作为一名创始人/CEO，关键在于没有人会来拯救你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your parents aren't going to rescue you, your VC is not going to rescue you, that kind of hits you when you hit your first crisis.
zh: 你的父母不会来拯救你，你的风投（VC）不会来拯救你，当你遇到第一次危机时，这种感觉会冲击你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Starting a company has never been easier, scaling one into a durable high impact organization has never been harder.
zh: 创办一家公司从未如此容易，将其扩展为一个持久、高影响力的组织也从未如此艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: The number of companies formed is going to much fewer over the next 10 years relative to the last 10 years, it's just going to be hard to stand out and really accelerate.
zh: 与过去 10 年相比，未来 10 年成立的公司的数量将会少得多，要想脱颖而出并真正实现加速将会很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's most different about what it was like to be a CEO maybe 10, 20 years ago versus today?
zh: 作为一名 CEO，现在与 10 年或 20 年前相比，最大的不同是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a massive tax in optionality when you can move this fast and try a lot of things.
zh: 当你能行动得这么快并尝试很多事情时，在选择权上会有巨大的负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: It puts pressure on the CEOs to be faster and better decision makers.
zh: 这给 CEO 们带来了压力，要求他们成为更快、更好的决策者。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people in the world want to be founders, they want to be CEOs.
zh: 世界上很多人想成为创始人，他们想成为 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think anyone can do it.
zh: 我认为不是任何人都能做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: People talk about 9-9-6, it's way more than that.
zh: 人们谈论 996，但这远不止于此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founders are seven days a week, they're always on, [inaudible 00:00:44] Sunday nights, it's full contact.
zh: 创始人是每周七天，他们时刻在线，周日晚上的[听不清 00:00:44]，这是全方位接触。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you feel like there are specific profiles or traits to be successful?
zh: 你觉得是否有特定的画像或特质才能获得成功？

speaker: Unknown
en: I look for four things, I call it my lock algorithm.
zh: 我看四样东西，我称之为我的锁定算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my guest is Brian Halligan, co-founder and longtime CEO of HubSpot.
zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Brian Halligan，HubSpot 的联合创始人兼长期 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked Brian to come on this podcast because he is, more than anyone I've met, a student of the job of a CEO.
zh: 我邀请 Brian 来这个播客是因为他比我见过的任何人都更像是一名研究 CEO 这一职位的学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: After leaving HubSpot last year, he became the in-house CEO coach at Sequoia, where he brings together dozens of top CEOs to learn from each other, he does one-on-one coaching with some of the world's top CEOs, he also hosts a popular podcast, called Long Strange Trip, where he interviews some of the world's most successful CEOs.
zh: 去年离开 HubSpot 后，他成为了红杉公司的内部 CEO 教练，在那里他召集了几十位顶级 CEO 互相学习，他与世界顶级的 CEO 中的一些人进行一对一辅导，他还主持一个受欢迎的播客，叫做 Long Strange Trip，他在那里采访世界上一些最成功的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this conversation, we unpack what it takes to be a successful CEO in today's era.
zh: 在这次对话中，我们将剖析在当今时代成为一名成功的 CEO 需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get into it, after a short word from our wonderful sponsors.
zh: 让我们开始吧，简短地感谢一下我们出色的赞助商之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Applications break in all kinds of ways, crashes, slowdowns, regressions, and the stuff that you only see once real users show up.
zh: 应用程序会以各种方式崩溃，崩溃、减速、回归，以及只有真正的用户出现时你才能看到的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sentry catches it all.
zh: Sentry 可以捕捉所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: See what happened where and why.
zh: 看看发生了什么，在哪里发生的，以及为什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Down to the commit that introduced the error, the developer who shipped it, and the exact line of code, all in one connected view.
zh: 直到引入错误的提交、运送它的开发人员，以及确切的代码行，所有这些都在一个 connected view 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've definitely tried the five tabs and Slack thread approach to debugging, this is better.
zh: 我肯定尝试过使用五个标签页和 Slack 线程来进行调试的方法，这个更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sentry shows you how the request moved, what ran, what slowed down, and what users saw.
zh: Sentry 向你展示请求是如何移动的，运行了什么，什么变慢了，以及用户看到了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seer, Sentry's AI debugging agent, takes it from there.
zh: Seer，Sentry 的 AI 调试智能体，会接管后续工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It uses all of that Sentry context to tell you the root cause, to adjust a fix, and even opens a PR for you.
zh: 它利用所有 Sentry 的上下文来告诉你根本原因，调整修复，甚至为你打开一个 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also reviews your PRs, and flags any breaking changes with fixes ready to go.
zh: 它还会审查你的 PR，并用准备好的修复标记任何破坏性的更改。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try Sentry and Seer for free at sentry.io/lenny, and use code Lenny for $100 in Sentry credits.
zh: 在 sentry.io/lenny 免费试用 Sentry 和 Seer，并使用代码 Lenny 获得 100 美元的 Sentry 积分。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's S-E-N-T-R-Y dot I-O/lenny.
zh: 那是 S-E-N-T-R-Y dot I-O/lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Datadog, now home to Eppo, the leading experimentation and feature flagging platform.
zh: 本集由 Datadog 为您带来，现在它是 Eppo 的归宿，Eppo 是领先的实验和功能标志平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Product managers at the world's best companies use Datadog, the same platform their engineers rely on every day to connect product insights to product issues, like bugs, UX friction, and business impact.
zh: 世界上最好公司的产品经理使用 Datadog，这是他们的工程师每天依赖的同一个平台，用于将产品洞察与产品问题（如错误、UX 摩擦和业务影响）联系起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It starts with product analytics, where PMs can watch replays, review funnels, dive into retention, and explore their growth metrics.
zh: 它始于产品分析，产品经理可以在那里观看回放、查看漏斗、深入留存率并探索他们的增长指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where other tools stop, Datadog goes even further.
zh: 在其他工具停止的地方，Datadog 走得更远。

speaker: Unknown
en: It helps you actually diagnose the impact of funnel drop-offs, and bugs, and UX friction.
zh: 它帮助你实际诊断漏斗流失、错误和 UX 摩擦的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you know where to focus, experiments prove what works.
zh: 一旦你知道了关注点在哪里，实验就会证明什么有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw this firsthand when I was at Airbnb, where our experimentation platform was critical for analyzing what worked and where things went wrong.
zh: 当我在 Airbnb 时，我亲眼看到了这一点，在那里我们的实验平台对于分析什么有效以及哪里出了问题是至关重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same team that built experimentation at Airbnb built Eppo.
zh: 在 Airbnb 建立实验的同一团队建立了 Eppo。

speaker: Unknown
en: Datadog then lets you go beyond the numbers with session replay.
zh: 然后 Datadog 让你通过会话回放超越数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Watch exactly how users interact with heatmaps and scroll maps to truly understand their behavior.
zh: 通过热力图和滚动图准确观察用户如何交互，以真正理解他们的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of this is powered by feature flags that are tied to real-time data, so that you can roll out safely, target precisely, and learn continuously.
zh: 所有这些都由与实时数据绑定的功能标志提供支持，因此你可以安全地推出、精确地定位并持续地学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Datadog is more than engineering metrics, it's where great product teams learn faster, fix smarter, and ship with confidence.
zh: Datadog 不仅仅是工程指标，它是优秀产品团队学得更快、修复得更聪明并充满信心地发布产品的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Request a demo at datadoghq.com/lenny, that's datadoghq.com/lenny.
zh: 在 datadoghq.com/lenny 申请演示，那是 datadoghq.com/lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brian, thank you so much for being here, and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Brian，非常感谢你来到这里，欢迎参加播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me, Lenny.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请，Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's my pleasure.
zh: 这是我的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with something that I've heard your board members, the way they described you, is someone with a perpetual state of constructive dissatisfaction.
zh: 我想从一些事情开始，我听到你的董事会成员描述你时，说你处于一种建设性不满的永恒状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think this is a core foundational trait of successful CEOs, successful leaders?
zh: 你认为这是成功 CEO、成功领导者的核心基本特质吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, I like that description, when she did, a woman named Lorrie Norrington, who [inaudible 00:04:26] said that.
zh: 顺便说一句，我喜欢这个描述，当她这样做时，一个叫 Lorrie Norrington 的女人，她[听不清 00:04:26]是这么说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like it, I took it as kind of a compliment, and I liked it.
zh: 我喜欢它，我把它当作一种赞美，而且我喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I spend most of my time these days coaching very fast-growth CEOs.
zh: 所以，这些天我大部分时间都在辅导非常快速增长的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all are kind of like that.
zh: 他们都有点像那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're all in kind of a state of perpetual dissatisfaction, but in a positive way.
zh: 他们都处于一种永恒的不满足状态，但是是以一种积极的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things, by the way, I like about the current crop of CEOs, they don't really take stock of what they've done and feel it, they're always a little bit dissatisfied with where they are, and very focused on the end state.
zh: 顺便说一句，我喜欢现在的这一批 CEO 的原因之一是，他们真的不怎么盘点他们做了什么并去感受它，他们总是对自己所处的位置有点不满足，并且非常关注最终状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've been surprised at how humble this generation is of CEOs.
zh: 而且我一直很惊讶这一代 CEO 是多么谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think of my generation of CEOs as being, I don't know, humble wasn't the first word that would come out of your mouth when you describe my generation.
zh: 我想到我那一代 CEO，我不知道，谦逊并不是在描述我那一代人时你会首先想到的词。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this generation I feel like is different, and I've been impressed with it.
zh: 但我觉得这一代人不同，我对此印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I have a bunch of questions along these lines, because one, you've been a CEO of an incredibly successful company for a long time, for about 20 years, before you moved on to this new chapter, now you work with a bunch of CEOs, you're Sequoia's in-house CEO coach, there's a few things that I've heard you do.
zh: 好的，我有一系列这方面的问题，因为第一，你在很长一段时间里是一家非常成功的公司的 CEO，大约 20 年，在你进入这个新篇章之前，现在你与一群 CEO 共事，你是红杉的内部 CEO 教练，我听说过你做的一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is you gather groups of CEOs, and what I've read is that you have kind of two tables.
zh: 一是你召集 CEO 们，我读到的是你有两种桌子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have the kids table and the adults table.
zh: 你有小孩桌和大人桌。

speaker: Unknown
en: The kids table is CEOs that are companies that are about under 100 employees, the adult table is over 100 employees.
zh: 小孩桌是公司员工大约 100 人以下的 CEO，大人桌是 100 人以上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let me ask you just, when you look at CEOs that move from the kids table to the adult table, other than just they scale and grow, what is it that these CEOs that graduate from kids to adults table do differently?
zh: 那么，我就问你，当你看着那些从小孩桌搬到大人桌的 CEO 时，除了他们扩大规模和成长之外，这些从小孩桌毕业到大人的 CEO 做了什么不同的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: The adults are really focused on, all they really want to talk about is their exec team.
zh: 大人们真的很专注于，他们真的只想谈论他们的高管团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their direct reports, how do you build our exec team, that next level down, org design... You would be surprised how much they think about that.
zh: 他们的直属下级，你们如何建立我们的高管团队，下一级往下，组织设计……你会惊讶于他们花多少心思在这上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on average, I would say the adults are spending half their time just recruiting and interviewing.
zh: 平均而言，我会说大人们把他们一半的时间都花在招聘和面试上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty all consuming.
zh: 这几乎是相当耗费精力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember that from that phase in HubSpot's growth.
zh: 我记得 HubSpot 增长阶段的那段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it surprises people like, wow, my job is really just to interview and hire, I didn't know that was going to be the case.
zh: 这让人们感到惊讶，哇，我的工作真的只是面试和招聘，我不知道会是这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that is one that they are making that transition, and I would just say in general, people are very bad at this, and HubSpot was too.
zh: 所以，这是他们正在做出的那个转变，我只想说总体上，人们非常不擅长这个，HubSpot 也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think CEOs and everyone dramatically overrates their ability to interview, and overrates their gut feeling, and underrates a really high quality blind reference.
zh: 我认为 CEO 和每个人都大大高估了他们面试的能力，并且高估了他们的直觉，而低估了真正高质量的盲测推荐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I interviewed Dave, the CEO from MongoDB the other day, and he had an interesting [inaudible 00:07:22].
zh: 我前两天采访了 Dave，MongoDB 的 CEO，他有一个有趣的 [听不清 00:07:22]。

speaker: Unknown
en: On average over his 10-year lifespan as a CEO of Mongo, there were two C-levels turned over per year.
zh: 平均在他担任 Mongo CEO 的 10 年生命周期中，每年有两位 C 级高管离职。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a lot of turnover at the top, and I didn't keep track of it like Dave, but I think HubSpot was kind of similar.
zh: 顶层的流失率很大，我没有像 Dave 那样追踪它，但我认为 HubSpot 有点类似。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of these startups are kind of similar too.
zh: 所有这些初创公司也都有点类似。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, people are working on that, and struggling with it, is one thing in common with all of them.
zh: 所以，人们正在为此努力，并为此挣扎，是他们的共同点之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do when you coach someone on that?
zh: 当你在那方面指导某人时你会做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're like, okay, you think you're amazing at interviewing, you think you know who's going to work out, what advice do you give them to help them develop that skill?
zh: 当你告诉他们，好吧，你认为自己面试很棒，你认为你知道谁会成功，你给他们什么建议来帮助他们培养那项技能？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think even me, I've been doing this for 150 years, I still think I overrate my ability to interview someone, and really know if they're a good fit.
zh: 我认为即使是我，我已经做了 150 年了，我仍然认为我高估了面试某人的能力，并且真的知道他们是否是一个好的人选。

speaker: Unknown
en: I give a couple pieces of advice.
zh: 我给出了几条建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Parker Conrad has a good hack that I liked.
zh: Parker Conrad 有一个我喜欢的好技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before he's got a C-level interview, CFO, chief product officer, whatever, he has some sign an NDA, and sends them the last board deck, or the board memo, or some important doc, and he schedules a half hour interview with them, and he just has a chat about the decks.
zh: 在他有 C 级面试之前，CFO、首席产品官之类的，他会让他们签署保密协议，并发给他们最新的董事会演示文稿，或董事会备忘录，或一些重要文档，他安排了半小时的面试，他只是和他们聊天关于那些演示文稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they're just very complimentary, and it's so great, and you're doing this amazing thing, it's a major red flag to him because he wants someone that will challenge him and not a yes person.
zh: 如果他们只是非常恭维，说这太棒了，你正在做这件惊人的事情，这对他说是一个主要的危险信号，因为他想要一个会挑战他而不是唯唯诺诺的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought that was a pretty good hack to get inside someone's head and how they think and how they'll interact with you.
zh: 我认为这是一个很好的技巧，可以进入某人的头脑，了解他们如何思考以及他们将如何与你互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting on a whiteboard and working through a problem I think is always a good thing.
zh: 我认为在白板上工作并解决一个问题总是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the standard interview of walking through your background, I don't think is all that valuable.
zh: 我认为标准的面试，走过你的背景，我认为并不是那么有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I coach people to do blind references, find someone you know that work with them... VCs are good at this by the way.
zh: 我指导人们做盲测推荐，找一个你知道与他们一起工作过的人……顺便说一下，风险投资人在这方面很擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I get a lot of these, and you can tell some of them are like, we've already decided we're checking the box, versus they're asking me hard questions about this person.
zh: 我收到了很多这样的，你可以看出其中一些像是，我们已经决定我们只是在打勾，对比他们问我关于这个人的难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of my favorite questions people ask is, would you enthusiastically rehire this person for that role?
zh: 人们问的我最喜欢的问题之一是，你会热情地重新雇佣这个人担任那个职位吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I think is a really good question.
zh: 我认为这是一个非常好的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: On a scale of one to 10, how likely is it that you'll try to rehire this person back from me down the road?
zh: 以 1 到 10 分为标准，你以后重新雇佣这个人的可能性有多大？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think those types of questions are good, so not mailing an in on those blind references I think is really good.
zh: 我认为这类问题是好的，所以在盲测推荐上不打勾我认为是非常好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: My other piece of advice, and no one listens to me on this, is hire slow and fire fast.
zh: 我的另一条建议，而且没人听我的，是慢聘快辞。

speaker: Unknown
en: People hire fast and fire slow.
zh: 人们快聘慢辞。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I had to guess, Lenny, with 18 months after you hire a C-level exec, at least 50% of the time they're gone.
zh: 如果我不得不猜，Lenny，在你雇佣 C 级高管后的 18 个月里，至少 50% 的时间他们都不在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: High mortality rate on them, it's harder than people think.
zh: 他们的死亡率很高，这比人们想象的要难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, what you're saying here is there's only so much you can actually do to increase those odds.
zh: 所以，你在这里说的是，实际上你只能做这么多来提高那些几率。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can, I think the blind references are key, I think doing real interactive, working on a project together is key.
zh: 我认为你可以，我认为盲测推荐是关键，我认为做真正的互动，一起在一个项目上工作是关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll tell you one of the things we learned at HubSpot about this.
zh: 我会告诉你在 HubSpot 我们学到的关于这一点的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would have a candidate come in, let's say a head of engineering, and we'd have eight people interview them.
zh: 我们会让一个候选人进来，比如说工程主管，我们会有八个人面试他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our scale's one to four.
zh: 我们的评分是一到四。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's say four people were four out of four, and four people were two out of four.
zh: 比如说四个人是四分之四，四个人是二分之四。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that's candidate A. And then the next candidate comes in, eight people interview them, and everyone's a three out of four.
zh: 所以，那是候选人 A。然后下一个候选人进来了，八个人面试他们，每个人都是四分里的三分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost every time we hired the three out of four, the person with the least amount of weaknesses.
zh: 几乎每次我们雇佣了那个四分三分的人，那个缺点最少的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we changed it, and we went with the spikier people, we went with people with weaknesses, we with people who would challenge stuff, and that has worked out quite well.
zh: 然后我们改变了做法，我们选择了那些更有棱角的人，我们选择了有缺点的人，我们选择了那些会挑战事情的人，结果相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our hit rate at HubSpot's improved.
zh: 我们在 HubSpot 的命中率提高了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have shrunk the pool of people on that interview panel from eight to four.
zh: 我们也把那个面试小组的人数从八人缩小到了四人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just hired a head of product, and there were just four of us that interviewed them.
zh: 我们刚雇佣了一位产品负责人，只有我们四个人面试了他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that worked too.
zh: 我认为那也奏效了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think there's things you can do to get better at it, for sure.
zh: 所以，我认为你可以做一些事情来做得更好，肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is incredibly tactical and useful.
zh: 这非常战术化且有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the references piece, the toughest part is getting people to be honest because there's very little upside to them to say negative things about people.
zh: 在推荐信这一块，最难的部分是让人们诚实，因为对他们来说说别人的坏处没什么好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything that you've learned to help get real honest answers from folks you call for references?
zh: 你有没有学到什么方法来帮助你从你打电话询问的推荐人那里得到真正诚实的回答？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I can just say I don't do this a lot anymore, but when people call me, I can tell if they've already decided, and when they're really just looking for... When they ask me for the strengths and weaknesses I'm like, oh, they've already decided.
zh: 嗯，我只能说我不怎么再做这事儿了，但是当人们打电话给我时，我能看出他们是否已经决定了，以及他们什么时候真的只是在寻找……当他们问优缺点时我就想，哦，他们已经决定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: When they ask me something hard, like on a scale of one to 10, how likely you're to hire them again?
zh: 当他们问我一些难的问题，比如从一分到十分，你有多可能再次雇佣他们？

speaker: Unknown
en: Stuff like that, that kind of gets at the core.
zh: 那样的事情，那种触及核心的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or were they the top 1% of your employees?
zh: 或者他们是你的员工中的前 1% 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good question.
zh: 那是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, were they top 10?
zh: 哦，他们是前 10% 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh.
zh: 哦。

speaker: Unknown
en: That type of question is pretty good.
zh: 那类型的问题相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, when I'm on the other side of it, I like when those types of questions come up.
zh: 所以，当我处于另一端时，我喜欢那些类型的问题出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I tell you the other mistake everyone makes, and all the CEOs we're making now, is you're hiring for that whatever, head of engineering, and you're blown away by the resume.
zh: 我告诉你大家犯的另一个错误，也是我们现在所有的 CEO 犯的，就是你在招聘那个……工程主管之类的，你被简历惊艳到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you're 50 employees and you're hiring this person, who's been at Microsoft the last 10 years, and has a fancy title, and is a fancy division in Microsoft, and you hire them, there's just a massive impedance mismatch when you hire them on what their expectations are, and what your expectations are, in the extent that you get your shit together.
zh: 就像你有 50 个员工，你雇佣这个人，他在微软待了最后 10 年，有一个花哨的头衔，在微软的一个花哨的部门，然后你雇佣了他们，这有一个巨大的阻抗不匹配，关于他们的期望是什么，以及你的期望是什么，在于你把你的事情搞定的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just you don't.
zh: 只是你没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: You definitely don't, if you're 50 or 500 employees.
zh: 你绝对没有，如果你是 50 或 500 名员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they expect you to have your act together.
zh: 而他们期望你有条不紊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that is another... Avoid the big company hire.
zh: 所以，这是另一个……避免从大公司雇佣。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hired so many people from Salesforce, and Google, and Microsoft, like 100% attrition rate on all those folks.
zh: 我们从 Salesforce、谷歌和微软雇佣了很多人，那些人的流失率是 100%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that I've seen that a lot of companies is there's phases of like, okay, now it's the McKinsey, a cohort comes in, and we think that's going to be the answer, and then it's the Apple group, and then that didn't work out, then the Amazon group.
zh: 我看到很多公司都有这种情况，就是有这样的阶段，好吧，现在是麦肯锡，一群人进来了，我们认为那将是答案，然后是苹果的那帮人，然后那没成功，然后是亚马逊的那帮人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The McKinsey one never works.
zh: 麦肯锡的那个从来都不奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: It never works.
zh: 它从来不奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: It never works.
zh: 它从来不奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: By definition, they would fail on my spectrum of... Most founders are like me, they are skeptical of dimensional wisdom, they're unhappy with the world works in some way, and so they're kind of far on that spectrum of rethinking dimensional wisdom.
zh: 根据定义，他们会在我的……光谱上失败……大多数创始人都像我，他们对传统的智慧持怀疑态度，他们对世界运作的某种方式不满意，所以他们在那个重新思考传统智慧的光谱上相当靠远。

speaker: Unknown
en: And almost by definition somebody who goes to work for McKinsey is very conservative in their outlook.
zh: 而且几乎根据定义，去为麦肯锡工作的人在他们观念上是非常保守的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I think that almost always fails.
zh: 所以，我认为这几乎总是失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're on this s hiring thread, so let me keep following this conversation.
zh: 我们既然在这个招聘线索上，那就让我继续这个对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I read somewhere that you recommend building your team like the 2004 Red Sox.
zh: 我在某处读到过你建议像 2004 年的红袜队那样组建你的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does this mean?
zh: 这是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I'm a big sports fan, a big Boston Red... And the Boston Red Sox hadn't won, Lenny, a World Series in 86 years, since they traded Babe Ruth.
zh: 嗯，我是个大体育迷，大波士顿红袜队……而波士顿红袜队还没赢过，Lenny，世界大赛在 86 年里，自从他们交易了 Babe Ruth 之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember that.
zh: 我记得那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they finally broke, and they finally won it in 2004.
zh: 然后他们终于打破了，他们终于在 2004 年赢得了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way they won it was they had a team of a bunch homegrown, really high quality, inexpensive talent that they drafted and came through the farm system.
zh: 他们赢得的方式是他们有一队本土培养的，真正高质量的，廉价的天才，他们选秀并通过农场系统培养出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they got a few free agents, like David Ortiz, that a lot of people have heard of, that they paid a fair amount of money to.
zh: 然后他们得到了几个自由球员，像 David Ortiz，很多人都听说过，他们付了相当多的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Peter Martinez and Curt Schilling were kind of the canonical older been there, done that, bigger company folks.
zh: Peter Martinez 和 Curt Schilling 有点像是典型的那种老牌的，经历过这些，大公司的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they mixed really nicely, the culture really worked.
zh: 他们混合得真的很好，文化真的奏效了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the key.
zh: 我认为那是关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people underrate their homegrown talent, almost across the board they underrate it.
zh: 我认为人们低估了他们的本土天才，几乎一贯地低估了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you want that mix.
zh: 我认为你想要那种混合。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to hire a whole bunch of been there, done that, and you don't want to hire [inaudible 00:14:57].
zh: 你不想雇佣一大帮经历过这些的人，你也不想雇佣 [听不清 00:14:57]。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine this is public, but you're now part owner of the Red Sox, is that right?
zh: 我想这是公开的，但你现在是红袜队的部分老板，对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I am a part owner of the Red Sox, yes.
zh: 我是红袜队的部分老板，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I have questions for you along those lines.
zh: 好的，我针对这方面有些问题要问你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, that's amazing advice.
zh: 好的，这建议太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of what I'm taking away here is people see all these fancy logos, amazing person, VP, this, that at Salesforce, Amazon, Google, whatever, and what you're saying here is don't underestimate the power of someone internal, rising to the occasion.
zh: 我在这里的理解是，人们看到所有这些花哨的标志，很棒的人，副总裁，这个，那个在 Salesforce，Amazon，Google，不管哪里，而你现在说的是不要低估内部人士的力量，挺身而出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at HubSpot, half the management team are folks who had been there for approximately 150 years, which I like.
zh: 如果你看看 HubSpot，一半的管理团队是那些在那里待了大约 150 年的人，我很喜欢这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And same with, you look at Apple, a lot of those people are homegrown.
zh: 同样的，你看苹果，那些人很多都是土生土长的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, is there any tips here for doing this well, is it just give people a chance?
zh: 那么，有什么做好这方面的技巧吗，就是只是给人们一个机会吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I tend to give people a chance.
zh: 我倾向于给人们一个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, if you're interviewing someone that's homegrown, and they're VP for that C-level job, versus hiring someone from the outside.
zh: 这就像，如果你正在面试一个土生土长的人，而且他们是那个 C 级工作的副总裁，相对于从外面雇佣一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hire someone from the outside, they're very good at interviewing, from a big company, they look fancy, they're shiny, you haven't seen their warts, hard to figure out their warts unless you're very good at line referencing, and so you tend to overrate them and underrate your homegrown.
zh: 我从外面雇佣一个人，他们非常擅长面试，来自大公司，他们看起来很花哨，他们很光鲜，你还没看到他们的缺点，很难弄清楚他们的缺点，除非你非常擅长引用参考，所以你倾向于高估他们并低估你的土生土长的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, if it's pretty close, I think you give your homegrown a shot at it.
zh: 所以，如果它很接近，我认为你给你的土生土长的人一个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's interesting to me, Lenny, is Brian Chesky sort of rethought a lot of this stuff, and he's like everyone's over-rotating to the homegrown to the experienced talent and management teams and delegation, I think he's mostly right about that.
zh: 对我来说很有趣的是，Lenny，Brian Chesky 重新思考了很多这些事情，他说大家都过度转向土生土长的人才，转向经验丰富的人才和管理团队以及授权，我认为他在这方面大部分是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: People haven't really followed that.
zh: 人们并没有真正遵循这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are, they're hiring people from the outside quite a bit.
zh: 人们是，他们相当多地从外面雇佣人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of the standard part of the playbook that all of them are following now.
zh: 这有点像他们现在都在遵循的标准剧本的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little different, it's actually quite different than what Brian [inaudible 00:16:32].
zh: 这有点不同，实际上这与 Brian [inaudible 00:16:32] 所说的相当不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Going back to the conversation around CEOs, a lot of people listening to this podcast, just a lot of people in the world want to be founders, they want to be CEOs.
zh: 回到关于 CEO 的对话，很多听这个播客的人，只是世界上很多人都想成为创始人，他们想成为 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, you look at Elon, you look at Jensen, you look at Steve Jobs, you look at you, a lot of people are like, I can't.
zh: 同时，你看看 Elon，你看看 Jensen，你看看 Steve Jobs，你看看你，很多人就像，我不能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not this person, I'm not going to be as good as them.
zh: 我不是这个人，我不会像他们一样好。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no world where I'm this good.
zh: 没有任何世界我会这么好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you feel like there are specific profiles or just traits that you have to be born with to be a successful CEO, or do you think it's earnable, anybody can be successful if they really work hard?
zh: 你觉得有特定的特征还是你必须与生俱来的特质才能成为成功的 CEO，或者你认为这是可获得的，任何人都可以成功，如果他们真的努力工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Go ahead and meet all these CEOs coming in, and I have a little algorithm in my head, and I look for four things.
zh: 继续去见所有这些进来的 CEO，我脑子里有一个小算法，我寻找四样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I call it my LOCK algorithm.
zh: 我称之为我的 LOCK 算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: L is for lovable, and Steve Jobs you would say is kind of rough and maybe not lovable, but he would inspire followership.
zh: L 代表可爱，Steve Jobs 你会说有点粗鲁，也许不可爱，但他会激发追随。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would want to follow him.
zh: 你会想要追随他。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, could I envision a 28-year-old me, graduating from business school, going to work for this person?
zh: 所以，我能想象一个 28 岁的我，从商学院毕业，去为这个人工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Would I crawl across broken glass?
zh: 我会爬过碎玻璃吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's question one.
zh: 那是问题一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two is just obsession.
zh: 第二只是痴迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they deeply obsessed with this problem?
zh: 他们对这个问题深深痴迷吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a little negative on people who came up with this problem to solve six months ago and started a company, I like people with deep founder market fit, who've been thinking about it for a long time, and have evidence in their lives of going deep down, obsessively down a rabbit hole because that's kind of what it takes to be a founder/CEO.
zh: 我对那些在六个月前想出这个问题要解决并创办了公司的人有点消极，我喜欢那些有深刻创始人市场契合度的人，那些已经思考了很长时间的人，并且有证据表明他们在生活中深入挖掘，痴迷地钻进兔子洞，因为这大概是成为创始人/CEO 所需要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The C is something I wouldn't have thought of, but this is a Sequoia thing, like chip on the shoulder.
zh: C 是一些我不会想到的东西，但这是 Sequoia 的事情，就像肩上的芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty much all of them have a boulder on their shoulder, and I have a bit of a chip on my shoulder too.
zh: 几乎所有人肩上都有一块巨石，我肩上也有点芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the K is just for deeply knowledgeable about the domain.
zh: 而 K 只是为了对领域有深刻了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I look for that.
zh: 所以，我寻找那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I were to stick an S on it, I would say student.
zh: 如果我要在上面加一个 S，我会说学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I look at Winston Weinberg from Harvey, or James from Profound, or Gabe from Rogo, some of these new very fast growing companies, they're students of the game.
zh: 我看看 Harvey 的 Winston Weinberg，或者 Profound 的 James，或者 Rogo 的 Gabe，这些新的非常快速增长的公司中的一些，他们是游戏的学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not just learn it alls, they're deep, deep, deep students of the game.
zh: 他们不仅仅是学习一切的人，他们是游戏的深刻、深刻、深刻的学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like LLMs, they're constantly, constantly learning, and it's not just learning stuff for me and their peers, but they go way back in time, and have a lot of history on stuff.
zh: 他们就像 LLMs，他们不断地、不断地学习，而且不只是为我而学东西，为他们的同龄人，但他们回到很久以前，对东西有很多历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, those are some of the, kind of my little criteria I use when I'm evaluating CEOs.
zh: 所以，这些是我在评估 CEO 时使用的一些我的小标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you look for, by the way, you've interviewed a ton of folks like me, what do you think is in common?
zh: 你寻找什么，顺便说一句，你面试了很多像我一样的人，你认为有什么共同点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Of what successful founders?
zh: 什么成功的创始人？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my god.
zh: 天啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish I had the... My succinct answer, I would go to Lennybot.com, and be like, what is the common pattern across these folks?
zh: 我希望我有……我的简洁回答，我会去 Lennybot.com，就像，这些人有什么共同模式？

speaker: Unknown
en: One that you didn't mention that I think is interesting, I did some research on this recently, with Terence Rohan, one is just extremely ambitious.
zh: 你没有提到的一个我认为很有趣的是，我最近对此做了一些研究，与 Terence Rohan 一起，一个就是非常有野心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just trying to do something really wild that most people are like, that's crazy.
zh: 只是尝试做一些真正疯狂的事情，大多数人就像，那太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to get a subscription service for all music in the world, that's just... What are you doing?
zh: 你不会为世界上所有的音乐获得订阅服务，这只是……你在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: [inaudible 00:19:38]-
zh: [inaudible 00:19:38]-

speaker: Unknown
en: [inaudible 00:19:40].

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it learnable?
zh: 它是可以学会的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I notice some of, a lot of the CEOs struggling with a couple of things.
zh: 我注意到一些，很多 CEO 在几件事上很挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like let's say you're Winston, you're late 20s, you've never managed a team, you're probably never even captain of a sports team before, and in order to scale, you have to give people feedback constantly.
zh: 比如说你是 Winston，你快 30 岁了，你从未管理过团队，你以前可能甚至从未当过运动队的队长，而且为了扩张，你必须不断地给别人反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very unnatural.
zh: 这非常不自然。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, I'm going to give this VP I hired a bunch of feedback, positive and negative.
zh: 这就像是，我要给我雇佣的这个 VP 一堆反馈，正面和负面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't get good at that, you really pay the price later.
zh: 如果你不擅长这个，你以后真的会付出代价。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something I think they have to learn.
zh: 我认为这是他们必须学会的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all have to learn to get a good bullshit detector.
zh: 他们都必须学会拥有一个好的废话探测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're constantly being spun, everyone's trying to sell to them, the org is always trying to sell to them.
zh: 他们不断地被忽悠，每个人都在试图向他们推销，组织总是试图向他们推销。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that's sort of something they have to develop over time.
zh: 所以，这是他们必须随着时间发展出来的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to all get good at the inspiration thing over time.
zh: 他们都必须随着时间的推移变得擅长鼓舞人心这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you're Winston, you've never had to inspire anyone in your entire life.
zh: 就像，你是 Winston，你这辈子从来没有鼓舞过任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You went to school, and you're a lawyer for a few years, and you started this thing... Inspiration wasn't your thing.
zh: 你去上学，当了几年律师，然后开始了这件事... 鼓舞人心不是你的强项。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, there's certain things you have to learn on that startup to scale up path, and the best ones learn it very fast.
zh: 所以，有一些东西他们必须在那条创业扩张的路上学会，最优秀的人学得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is extremely interesting and useful.
zh: 这非常有趣和有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, LOCK, with an S at the end, just to kind of mirror back what you're sharing.
zh: 所以，LOCK，末尾有个 S，只是为了回溯一下你分享的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you were saying you evaluate CEOs, is this for investing as a-
zh: 当你说你评估 CEO 时，这是为了投资而-

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so when you're helping Sequoia decide should we invest in this company, what you look for is, LOCK... I like the S, I'm going to include it there.
zh: 好的，所以当你帮助 Sequoia 决定我们是否应该投资这家公司时，你寻找的是，LOCK... 我喜欢这个 S，我要把它包含在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, are they lovable?
zh: 所以，他们讨人喜欢吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they inspiring?
zh: 他们鼓舞人心吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: O, are they obsessed with this problem they're going after?
zh: O，他们对自己正在解决的问题着迷吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they have a chip on their shoulder?
zh: 他们心里有气吗？

zh: 其中很多都是老生常谈，公司死于暴食的可能性远大于死于消化不良。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually it was when we were trying to do too much.
zh: 通常是因为我们试图做得太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't heard that version, I've always heard most companies die have suicide versus homicide.
zh: 我没听过这个版本，我常听到的是大多数公司的死因是自杀而不是他杀。

speaker: Unknown
en: Though indigestion-
zh: 虽然关于消化不良——

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true too, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句，那也是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh man.
zh: 噢天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so next Halliganism, "Never waste a good crisis."
zh: 好了，下一个 Halliganism，“永远不要浪费一场好危机。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that people hear, I'm curious just what's the lesson here, and then is there an example of this where you learned this lesson?
zh: 这是人们常听到的，我很好奇这里的教训是什么，然后有没有一个你学到这个教训的例子？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll just follow on to, most of the good things that happened in HubSpot came out of a crisis because we would take pretty drastic measures to fix it and make sure we didn't do the same thing again.
zh: 我接着刚才的说，HubSpot 发生的大多数好事都源于危机，因为我们会采取相当激进的措施来修复它，并确保我们不会再做同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, in this particular case, we really rethought how we deployed software, how we thought about making software in a way that was incredibly healthy.
zh: 所以，在这个特定的案例中，我们真正重新思考了我们如何部署软件，我们如何考虑以一种非常健康的方式制作软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we haven't had a serious outage since.
zh: 从那以后，我们再没有发生过严重的故障。

speaker: Unknown
en: The quality is much better.
zh: 质量好多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of an interesting thing with HubSpot is we started as a marketing software company, and we pivoted, had Salesforce came into our market, we pivoted into CRM.
zh: 关于 HubSpot 有一点很有趣，我们起初是一家营销软件公司，然后我们转型了，Salesforce 进入了我们的市场，我们转型进入了 CRM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that... If your marketing software goes down, if your workflow, if there's a bug in the workflows or something like that, it's bad, but you survive it, you wait a little bit.
zh: 有一件事……如果你的营销软件宕机了，如果你的工作流，如果工作流中有错误或类似的情况，这很糟糕，但你还能挺过去，你只需稍等片刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your CRM goes down, particularly on the last day of the quarter, you're really impacting your customer's ability to do business.
zh: 如果你的 CRM 宕机了，特别是在季度的最后一天，你真的会影响你客户开展业务的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, that was a mindset shift that we hadn't quite come to terms with of how important we were to our customers.
zh: 所以，那是我们尚未完全接受的一种思维转变，即我们要对我们的客户有多重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, we made a lot of changes based on that crisis.
zh: 所以，基于那次危机，我们做出了很多改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually very good things came out of crises.
zh: 通常，好事都源于危机。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, there's the lesson there, something's going wrong, is it just like over-correct?
zh: 所以，这里有一个教训，出了问题，是不是只是矫枉过正？

speaker: Unknown
en: Use this as a way to-
zh: 把这当作一种方式来——

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always over-corrected.
zh: 我们总是会矫枉过正。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we almost, we purposely swung the pendulum hard the other way.
zh: 是的，我们几乎，我们是有意将钟摆用力摆向另一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which connects to the first Halliganism of, "If you're eating a shit sandwich, don't nibble."
zh: 这与第一个 Halliganism 相关联，“如果你在吃屎三明治，不要小口咬。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost like go all the way, go even further.
zh: 这几乎意味着一路走下去，甚至更进一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make it really obvious to everyone what's going on.
zh: 让每个人都清楚到底发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, another Halliganism, "If you want to kill a plant, have two people water it."
zh: 好了，另一个 Halliganism，“如果你想弄死一株植物，就让两个人去浇它。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this one, it's very true.
zh: 我喜欢这一条，非常真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say, Lenny, you bought a new beautiful plant for your office, and then you went away for a month to Turks and Caicos because your AI agent's doing your podcast, and you asked two of your friends, "Hey, would you mind watering my plant?"
zh: 比如说，Lenny，你为你的办公室买了一株漂亮的新植物，然后你离开一个月去 Turks and Caicos，因为你的 AI 智能体正在做你的播客，你问你的两个朋友，“嘿，你们能帮我浇一下植物吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's one of two outcomes what happens to the plant.
zh: 接下来植物会有两种结果之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: The plant would either be over-watered and die, or not watered at all and die.
zh: 植物要么被淹死，要么完全没被浇水而死。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every CEO in the adults' table has gone through this, and they are religious about the DRI.
zh: 成年人桌边的每一位 CEO 都经历过这种事，而且他们对 DRI 极度执着。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone talks about DRI in the kids' table, but once it gets to the adults' table, people get deep religion on it.
zh: 小孩桌边的每个人都在谈论 DRI，但一旦到了成年人桌边，人们就会对它深信不疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it makes sense.
zh: 我认为这有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're small, and you're in startup mode, everyone's in the room, everyone knows exactly what's going on.
zh: 当你规模很小，处于创业模式时，每个人都在同一个房间里，每个人都确切地知道发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let's say you're running a pilot project with a big account.
zh: 所以，假设你正在与一个大客户运行一个试点项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're running that pilot project, everyone's on the same page, the sales person, the service person, developer, everyone's on the same page, and you go out and do it and you execute well.
zh: 你正在运行那个试点项目，每个人都在同一频道上，销售人员、服务人员、开发人员，每个人都在同一频道上，然后你们出去做这件事，并且执行得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you get it scale, you've get a sales organization, you've get your [inaudible 00:44:56] deployed engineer organization, you've got your product management organization, you've got some developers working on it.
zh: 当你达到一定规模时，你有了销售组织，你有了部署工程师组织，你有了产品管理组织，你有一些开发人员在为此工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's kind of separate, no one knows really what's going on in the other departments.
zh: 每个人都有些分离，没有人真正知道其他部门里在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, let's say you want to really have a good pilot process, you want to rethink it because you're scaling.
zh: 所以，假设你真的想有一个好的试点流程，因为你正在规模化，所以你想重新思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything important happens cross-functionally inside a company at scale, and you need someone powerful to own it.
zh: 在规模化的公司内部，所有重要的事情都是跨职能发生的，你需要一个有权势的人来拥有它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let's say it's a sales person, they need the power to tell people in other divisions what to do, even if they don't own it.
zh: 所以，假设这是一个销售人员，他们需要权力去告诉其他部门的人做什么，即使他们并不拥有那个部门。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, almost every CEO I deal with is like a zealot on the DRI idea, and it doesn't bite you until you get to some sort of scale.
zh: 所以，我打交道的几乎每一位 CEO 都像是一个 DRI 理念的狂热信徒，而且直到你达到某种规模时它才会咬你（让你吃亏）。

speaker: Unknown
en: To be super clear about that advice here, it's one person is responsible for a goal, a metric, some outcome you want, versus it may feel like, okay, we have two people on this, it'll be awesome, they'll work together.
zh: 为了在这里把那个建议说得非常清楚，就是一个人对一个目标、一个指标、一个你想要的结果负责，而不是感觉像这样，好的，我们有两人在这个上面，这会很棒，他们会一起工作。

speaker: Brian Halligan
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your advice here is that doesn't work?
zh: 你这里的建议是那行不通？

speaker: Unknown
en: Communities never work.
zh: 委员会永远行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And DRI is directly responsible individual.
zh: 而 DRI 指的是直接责任人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I always thought about this is just having someone's ass on the line for something makes them so motivated to get it done, versus spreading the responsibility and the upside and the downside, it just doesn't work.
zh: 我对此的一贯想法是，让某人的屁股为某件事悬着会让他们如此有动力去完成它，相比之下分散责任、收益和风险，是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I totally agree with you.
zh: 我完全同意你的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, another Halliganism, I don't know if you put it this way, the way I think about it is this idea of, "There's no such thing as a silver bullet, it just takes a lot of lead bullets to get something done."
zh: 好的，另一个哈里根主义，我不知道你是否是这么说的，我对这个问题的思考方式是，这个理念是，“没有什么灵丹妙药，它只需要大量的实弹来把事情做成。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the way you wrote about it is it's always one step forward, two steps back.
zh: 我认为你描述它的方式是，总是进一步，退两步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about your advice there.
zh: 谈谈你在那方面的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I always thought, incorrectly, that we would have one hire or one investor or one event or one product release that would... I was wrong about this, but it'd be a silver bullet.
zh: 是的，我总是错误地以为，我们会通过一次招聘、一位投资者、一个事件或一次产品发布来……我在这件事上错了，但这会是一颗银弹。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reality inside the HubSpot machine, the way it felt to me, it looks from the outside, over a long time up into the right, and smooth, but inside it was two steps forward, one step back, two steps forward, one step back, two steps forward, one step back.
zh: 而在 HubSpot 机器内部的现实，对我来说感觉是这样，从外部看，在很长一段时间里，它是向右上方且平滑的，但在内部它是进一步，退一步，进一步，退一步，进一步，退一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of times it was a crisis that caused that step back.
zh: 而且很多时候是一场危机导致了那退后的一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, we just didn't have that.
zh: 所以，我们没有那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing about being a founder/CEO is no one, especially when you're in your 20s, there's no one there to rescue you.
zh: 作为创始人/CEO 的事情是，没有人，特别是当你 20 多岁时，那里没有人来拯救你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your parents aren't going to rescue you, your VC is not going to rescue you, your teacher, your thesis advisor, you're on your own and you got to figure it out.
zh: 你的父母不会来救你，你的 VC 不会来救你，你的老师，你的论文导师，你都要靠你自己，你必须把它搞清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that hits you when you hit your first crisis, it's on you.
zh: 当你遇到第一次危机时这会打击到你，这取决于你。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get some help, but it's on you.
zh: 你可以得到一些帮助，但这取决于你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes they have you in their corner, if they're lucky at Sequoia.
zh: 有时他们会在你这边，如果他们有幸在红杉资本的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plug, plug.
zh: 插播广告，插播广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't solve it oftentimes, I can be the shoulder they cry on, and I can give them advice, but it's still on them.
zh: 我经常无法解决它，我可以成为他们哭泣的肩膀，我可以给他们建议，但这仍然取决于他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you feel like too many people start companies just like... When someone comes to you like, hey Brian, should I start a company?
zh: 你觉得是不是太多人创办公司就像……当有人来找你，嘿 Brian，我应该创办一家公司吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I have this idea.
zh: 我有这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you often just like, no.
zh: 你经常只是，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have no idea what you're getting into, this is going to be much more painful?
zh: 你不知道你要陷入什么，这会比那痛苦得多？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard Jensen Huang say that.
zh: 我听 Jensen Huang 这么说过。

speaker: Unknown
en: "I wouldn't have start started Nvidia if I had it to do over."
zh: “如果我要重新来过，我不会创办 Nvidia。”

speaker: Unknown
en: If someone asked me that question, I would start HubSpot over.
zh: 如果有人问我那个问题，我会重新创办 HubSpot。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very hard, there were a lot of sacrifices, it wasn't glamorous at all.
zh: 那很难，有很多牺牲，一点也不光鲜。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the end of the day, I'm incredibly proud of it.
zh: 但归根结底,我对此感到无比自豪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on my deathbed, I can look back and really enjoy it.
zh: 在我的临终时,我可以回首往事并真正享受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the Dalai Lama's got a good expression like, "Live a good life so you can live it again on your deathbed."
zh: 达赖喇嘛有一句很好的话,「过好生活,这样你才能在临终时再过一遍。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm really glad I did it.
zh: 我真的很高兴我这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do talk a lot of founders out of it.
zh: 但我确实劝退了很多创始人不要这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: The obsession is real, you have to be deeply obsessed.
zh: 这种痴迷是真实的,你必须深深地痴迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all these founders and CEOs I talk to, people talk about 9-9-6, it's way more than that.
zh: 所有与我交谈过的创始人和 CEO,人们谈论 996,但这比那要更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founders are seven days a week, they're always on, I [inaudible 00:48:40] on Sunday nights, it's full contact.
zh: 创始人们是一周七天,他们随时待命,我在周日晚上的[听不清 00:48:40],这是全方位接触的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what's going on there, particularly now, is people just see this massive platform change, massive opportunity, they don't want to waste the opportunity.
zh: 我认为现在发生的情况是,人们只是看到了这个巨大的平台变革、巨大的机会,他们不想浪费这个机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that mindset's right.
zh: 所以,我认为这种心态是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people today are much, much more hardcore than they were in my year.
zh: 但今天的人们比我那个年代的人们要硬核得多,多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked hard, and I was probably, I was 60 to 70 week hours a week the entire time, never really turned it off.
zh: 我工作很努力,我可能整个时间每周工作 60 到 70 小时,从未真正关机过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's kind of how I thought about it.
zh: 但我就是那样思考的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's different now.
zh: 现在不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are much more focused, and I think Elon's inspired people.
zh: 人们更加专注,我认为 Elon 激励了人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a start back in the day, nowhere near as successful as HubSpot, but the way I thought about it is, let me just give it everything I have and see what I can do.
zh: 我早年有过一次创业,远没有 HubSpot 成功,但我当时的思考方式是,让我全力以赴,看看我能做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the shot, this is my chance, let me just give it all.
zh: 这就是机会,这是我的机会,让我倾尽所有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Forget balance, just go for it.
zh: 忘掉平衡,只管去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seven days a week for a while.
zh: 一段时间内一周七天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you scale back.
zh: 然后你就会缩减规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just such an empowering thing to do for a while, just like, let me just try.
zh: 在一段时间内,这是一件非常赋能的事情,就像说,让我只是尝试一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: This won't be forever.
zh: 这不会永远持续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know you've written about this, just like balance for CEO is not, you should not have work-life balance if you want to be incredibly successful.
zh: 我知道你写过这个,就像 CEO 的平衡不是,如果你想获得巨大的成功,你不应该有工作与生活的平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if that's always true, but just... I don't know, how do you talk about that to founders?
zh: 我不知道这是否总是正确的,但是……我不知道,你如何与创始人谈论这个?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know any of the founders I work with that have work-life balance.
zh: 我与我共事的创始人中,我不知道有谁拥有工作与生活的平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, this is not something I recommend.
zh: 顺便说一下,这不是我推荐的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't have it, I don't think my co-founder, Dharmesh had it.
zh: 我没有,我不认为我的联合创始人 Dharmesh 有。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only CEO I know, and he's unusual in this way, is Kareem from Clay.
zh: 我认识的唯一 CEO,他在这方面很不同寻常,是 Clay 的 Kareem。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, "Nope, you need balance, take the weekends..." He's got a different mindset.
zh: 他就像,「不,你需要平衡,周末休息……」他有一种不同的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to have him on my pod to talk about his mindset.
zh: 我打算请他上我的播客来谈谈他的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he's sort of the outlier, everyone else is really, really obsessed, and they really don't have much of a life.
zh: 但他算是异类,其他人都真的、真的很痴迷,他们真的没有太多的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: It did take them a long time to find product market fit [inaudible 00:50:25]-
zh: 他们确实花了很长时间找到产品市场契合[听不清 00:50:25]

speaker: Unknown
en: [inaudible 00:50:25] definitely pre-AI.
zh: [听不清 00:50:25] 绝对是在 AI 之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: It did them a long...
zh: 他们确实花了很长……

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder if there's a correlation, but it did work out.
zh: 我想知道是否存在相关性,但这确实行得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Worked out great.
zh: 结果很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it is a good lesson.
zh: 所以,这是一个很好的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, a few more here.
zh: 好的,这里还有几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, it's a math formula.
zh: 一个是,它是一个数学公式。

speaker: Unknown
en: "EV is greater than TV is greater than MEV."
zh: 「EV 大于 TV 大于 MEV。」

speaker: Unknown
en: What is that?
zh: 那是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, EV is enterprise value, TV is your team's value, MEV is your value.
zh: 好的,EV 是企业价值,TV 是你团队的价值,MEV 是你的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as HubSpot was scaling, and we had a lot of people who were VPs in different roles, and they started to get good-sized organizations, where they would fall down was they didn't solve for MEV, but they'd solve for TV over EV.
zh: 随着 HubSpot 的扩张,我们有很多担任不同职位副总裁的人,他们开始拥有相当规模的团队,他们跌倒的地方在于他们没有解决 MEV,而是为了 TV 解决而牺牲了 EV。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'd solve for their own team.
zh: 他们是为了他们自己的团队解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, let's say they ran sales, and say, I just want bookings to be as high as possible because I get paid on bookings, and the service team can handle all the downstream problems I created.
zh: 所以,假设他们负责销售,并说,我只是希望预订量尽可能高,因为我是根据预订量获得报酬的,服务团队可以处理我制造的所有下游问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Marketing to sales... Between every department that's happened.
zh: 从市场营销到销售……在每个部门之间都发生过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the kind of immature managers who didn't scale, really solved for themselves, and as they solved for themselves kind of sub-optimize for their peers.
zh: 那种未能扩张的不成熟管理者,真的只是为了自己解决,而且当他们为了自己解决时,会为了他们的同伴进行次优优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And their employees would notice it and complain about it, it would be fine in the short term, but it would show up.
zh: 他们的员工会注意到这一点并抱怨它,这在短期内会没事,但最终会暴露出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the place it would show up, Lenny, was, we did, and I think a lot of companies do this now, but we did a quarterly employee net promoter.
zh: Lenny,它暴露的地方是,我们做了,我认为很多公司现在也这样做,但我们做了季度员工净推荐值。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did a quarterly customer net promoter survey and a quarterly employee one.
zh: 我们做了季度客户净 promoters 调查和季度员工调查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we would have people rate it by the department they're in.
zh: 我们会让人按他们所在的部门来评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one interesting thing about that, so it's like sales and service and engineering, all the different departments, and we had an overall net promoter score, and then each department had a net promoter score.
zh: 关于这点有一个有趣的现象，比如销售部、服务部、工程部，所有不同的部门，我们要有一个整体的净 promoters 分数，然后每个部门都有一个净 promoters 分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's just take sales.
zh: 我们就拿销售部来说吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sales net promoter score was like, 65, 62, 68, 30.
zh: 销售部的净 promoters 分数是像，65，62，68，30。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ooh, that's a big drop.
zh: 噢，那是大幅下跌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you read the comments and it was not good, a lot of complaints about the leader of that.
zh: 然后你阅读那些评论，情况并不好，有很多关于那负责人的抱怨。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the complaints were a little bit of this TV thing.
zh: 很多抱怨都有点像这个 TV 的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, we give feedback to that VP, would help them, we give them all the comments, be like, you got this.
zh: 然后，我们给那位 VP 反馈，会帮助他们，我们把所有的评论都给他们，就像说，你收到了这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a quarter later from 30 to -5.
zh: 然后一个季度后，从 30 变成了 -5。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they almost never actually recovered.
zh: 他们几乎从未真正恢复过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you lose, your team can't... It's hard to get them back.
zh: 当你输了，你的团队不能……很难让他们回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why I say hire slow, fire fast.
zh: 这就是我说聘用要慢，解雇要快的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this doesn't show up in the first 100, 150 employees, everyone's solving for EV, but as it gets bigger, and the CEO doesn't know anyone, and there's a couple layers between you and the employees, they tend to solve for TV.
zh: 这在最初的 100、150 名员工中不会显现，每个人都在为 EV 而努力，但随着公司变大，CEO 不认识任何人，而且你和员工之间有几层层级，他们倾向于为 TV 而努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, we always put on the wall, "Solve for EV over TV over MEV," and then we added CV in front of EV, solve for the customers first, then for HubSpot, then the employee, then yourself.
zh: 所以，我们总是把「解决 EV 优先于 TV 优先于 MEV」贴在墙上，然后我们在 EV 前面加了 CV，首先为客户解决，然后为 HubSpot，然后是员工，最后是你自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was be very helpful to us.
zh: 这对我们非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I imagine everybody listening, working at a big company understands this.
zh: 是的，我想每个在听的人，在一家大公司工作的人都理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where you have goals, you get your KPIs, and your performance reviews based on what impact you drive, if you hit your goals.
zh: 你有目标，你得到你的 KPI，还有你的绩效评估是基于你驱动的影响，如果你达成了你的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, the incentives are focused on my goals and drive those, and I don't care about other people's goals, the company's goals-
zh: 所以，激励机制集中在我的目标和驱动这些目标上，我不在乎其他人的目标，公司的目标——

speaker: Unknown
en: Steve Jobs had an interesting line, he says, "You don't work for your boss, you work for Apple."
zh: Steve Jobs 有一个有趣的说法，他说，「你不是为你的老板工作，你是为 Apple 工作。」

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought that was pretty good.
zh: 我觉得那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I heard that after I was CEO of HubSpot, but that kind of captures the sentiment.
zh: 我是在我担任 HubSpot CEO 之后才听到的，但这确实捕捉到了那种情感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how I felt about HubSpot.
zh: 我对 HubSpot 也有这种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You work for HubSpot first and then you work for your boss.
zh: 你首先为 HubSpot 工作，然后才是为你的老板工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is hard because people's performance reviews are based on their goals, KPIs, it's always like, here's what I got to drive.
zh: 这很难，因为人们的绩效评估是基于他们的目标、KPI，总是像，这是我要驱动的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other than putting posters on the wall, and this is our, just HubSpot growth above all is what matters, or our customers, I guess in your case.
zh: 除了在墙上贴海报，也就是我们的，HubSpot 的增长高于一切才是重要的，或者是我们的客户，我想在你的情况下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything tactically that was useful in helping people prioritize enterprise value?
zh: 在帮助人们确定企业价值优先级方面，有什么战术上的有用之处吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This was explicitly called out in the form for the employee when you got your review, this was part of it.
zh: 这在员工获得评估的表格中被明确指出了，这是其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, they get a score of one to, I forget, 10 on that.
zh: 所以，他们会得到一个 1 到，我忘了，10 的分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would talk about it constantly.
zh: 我会不断地谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we first started HubSpot, I ran it a little bit like Jensen runs NVIDIA, where I didn't do one-on-ones, and I gave a lot of good and bad feedback publicly in large management team meetings, and I definitely would go out of my way to criticize people if I felt like they were solving for TV over EV.
zh: 当我们刚开始 HubSpot 时，我运行得有点像 Jensen 运行 NVIDIA 那样，我不做一对一，我在大型管理团队会议上公开发布很多好的和坏的反馈，如果我觉得他们在为 TV 而不是 EV 解决，我绝对会特意批评他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people got a sense for that.
zh: 人们对此有感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, every quarter we did a really well-produced company meeting, we spent a lot of time on it, and at the end of the company meeting, we gave out, we called them the Champaigner Awards, it was a bottle of Veuve, that my co-founder and I signed.
zh: 然后，每个季度我们要举行一次制作精良的公司会议，我们花了很多时间在上面，在公司会议结束时，我们要颁发，我们称之为 Champaigner 奖，那是一瓶 Veuve，是我的联合创始人和我签名的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'd read something nice about them and give it to them, and usually there was an EV team in that.
zh: 我们会读一些关于他们的好东西并给他们，通常那里会有一个 EV 团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, we did different things to kind of beat that into people's heads.
zh: 所以，我们做了不同的事情，想把它灌输到人们的脑子里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 真棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, here is just celebrate people that focus on this, and also included in their valuation performance reviews.
zh: 所以，这里只是庆祝那些专注于这一点的人，并且也包括在他们的估值绩效评估中。

speaker: Brian Halligan
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good segue to another Halliganism where you talk about how companies are either customer-centric or investor-centric, and it's really important to know which you are.
zh: 这是另一个 Halligan 主义的一个很好的过渡，你谈到公司要么是以客户为中心，要么是以投资者为中心，知道你是哪一种非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you guys actually shifted there.
zh: 你们实际上在那里进行了转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your insight there?
zh: 你对此有什么见解？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were very employee-centric, more than customer-centric in the first several years of HubSpot.
zh: 在 HubSpot 的最初几年里，我们非常以员工为中心，而不是以客户为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much so that the company was number one on Glassdoor's best place to work, I was the number one CEO on Glassdoor, and as I look back at that, I'm not sure that's a good thing.
zh: 甚至到了公司在 Glassdoor 最佳工作场所排名第一，我是 Glassdoor 上的第一 CEO，现在回头看，我不确定那是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wanting to be liked I don't think is a good feature of a CEO, and wanting to be the best place to work probably isn't the right way to go.
zh: 想要被喜欢我不认为是 CEO 的一个好特质，想要成为最佳工作场所可能也不是正确的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at Toby from Shopify, his scores aren't that good, but that company is doing really, really well.
zh: 如果你看看 Shopify 的 Toby，他的分数没那么好，但那家公司真的做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, we over-indexed on it, and part of the reason we over-indexed on it is my co-founder was really strong in this, and we had an incredibly powerful head of HR, named Katie Burke, and we just worked on it.
zh: 所以，我们在这方面过度投入了，过度投入的部分原因是我的联合创始人在这方面真的很强，我们有一位非常强大的人力资源负责人，名叫 Katie Burke，我们就在那上面下功夫。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spent a lot of time on it.
zh: 我们在那上面花了很多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we'd have a management team meeting, and let's say it's four hours long, two of the four hours would be on employee stuff.
zh: 当我们召开管理团队会议时，假设是四个小时，四个小时里有两个小时是关于员工的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at some point I was like, why are we spending so much time on employee net promoter scores?
zh: 在某个时刻我想说，为什么我们要在员工净推荐值上花这么多时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say our employee net promoter score was 60, and our customer net promoter score is 25, I was like, we need to take... I would give up 10 points of employee net promoter score to get 10 points of customer net promoter score.
zh: 假设我们的员工净推荐值是 60，而我们的客户净推荐值是 25，我想，我们需要拿……我愿意牺牲 10 点员工净推荐值来换取 10 点客户净推荐值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, over some time we shifted the center of gravity to customers, and we still of course, worried about employees, but the center of gravity from HubSpot moves very much to customers.
zh: 所以，过了一段时间，我们把重心转移到了客户身上，我们当然仍然担心员工，但 HubSpot 的重心非常明显地转移到了客户身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did that in a few ways.
zh: 我们通过几种方式做到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time we had a management team meeting... We had our management team meetings once a month, not once a week, and we would have a customer panel come on, and that customer panel, I would run the panel, and ask very tricky questions to the customers, and pull out the bad news from that.
zh: 每次我们召开管理团队会议……我们的管理团队会议是一个月一次，而不是一周一次，我们会请来一个客户小组，我会主持这个小组，向客户提出非常刁钻的问题，并从中挖掘坏消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, we still do this, we have a customer panel at our board meetings.
zh: 然后，我们至今仍在这样做，我们在董事会会议上也有客户小组。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our whole board can ask questions.
zh: 我们的整个董事会都可以提问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my favorite question is, what do you love about HubSpot?
zh: 我最喜欢的问题是，你喜欢 HubSpot 的什么地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then... And then, what do you hate about HubSpot?
zh: 然后……然后，你讨厌 HubSpot 的什么地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they kind of look at their shoes.
zh: 他们看着自己的鞋子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, come on.
zh: 你就像是在说，拜托。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a great way... So, the employee's voice is here, those company meetings, we have the customers at the company meetings.
zh: 这是一个很好的方式……所以，员工的声音在这里，在公司会议里，我们有客户参加公司会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: We changed the comp plan, so the management team got paid not on revenue but on retention and net promoter score.
zh: 我们改变了薪酬计划，所以管理团队的薪酬不是基于收入，而是基于留存率和净推荐值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we worked very hard and swung the pendulum to customer-centric.
zh: 所以我们非常努力地工作，把钟摆摆向以客户为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think companies have one center of gravity or another.
zh: 但我确实认为公司都有这个重心或那个重心。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a really interesting thread throughout this conversation of just, when do you want to change how you operate you have to go really far to a whole other... And to almost over-correct to... Yeah, it's a really interesting of just how much work it takes to change culture, to change your norms.
zh: 在整个对话中有一个非常有趣的线索，就是，当你想改变你的运营方式时，你必须走到完全不同的另一个……而且几乎要过度纠正到……是的，这是非常有趣的，就是改变文化、改变你的规范需要付出多少努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the bigger it is, the more obvious you have to make it.
zh: 而且规模越大，你必须表现得越明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing about being a CEO, Lenny, is you got to say the same thing over and over and over and over and over again.
zh: 关于做 CEO 的另一件事是，Lenny，你必须一遍又一遍又一遍又一遍又一遍地说同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just doesn't sink into people's heads, you have to just be incredibly repetitive on it before it sinks in.
zh: 它就是进不到人们的脑子里，你必须非常重复地讲它，它才会深入人心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same thing with marketing, but internally, and that happens.
zh: 营销也是一样，但是在内部，这会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other weird thing about being a CEO, Lenny, is as it gets bigger... When it's small, everyone's giving you shit, and you're all on the same level.
zh: 关于做 CEO 的另一件奇怪的事情是，Lenny，随着公司变大……当它很小的时候，每个人都在给你提意见，你们都处在同一水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as it gets bigger, you didn't interview everyone, you have thousands of employees, you don't know everyone, and people put you on a pedestal that you don't deserve.
zh: 但随着它变大，你没有面试过每个人，你有数千名员工，你不认识每个人，而且人们把你放在一个你不配的基座上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's say you're in the hallway, and you're just kind of shooting the shit with a bunch of people, and you're like, ah, it'd be cool if we had a product that did... Somebody inevitably would go home and build that thing, and be like, Brian wants this as a big initiative.
zh: 假设你在走廊里，只是和一群人闲聊，你说，啊，如果我们有一个做……的产品会很酷，有人不可避免地会回家去构建那个东西，然后说，Brian 希望把这作为一个重大举措。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, people really lock in on what you said.
zh: 所以，人们真的会锁定你所说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out you have to be very repetitive and you have to be very careful what you say.
zh: 事实证明，你必须非常重复，而且你必须对你所说的话非常小心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dharmesh was on the podcast, your illustrious co-founder, and he developed a whole system to avoid this sort of thing.
zh: Dharmesh 来过这个播客，你这位杰出的联合创始人，他开发了一整套系统来避免这种事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Flash tags, where it's like, this is just an FYI.
zh: Flash 标签，就像这样，这只是一个仅供参考。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a whole system.
zh: 我们有一整套系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we would say something on an email to the management team, or Slack, and everyone would be like, okay, this is what they want, let's do it.
zh: 因为我们会在发给管理团队的电子邮件或 Slack 上说些什么，然后每个人都会说，好吧，这就是他们想要的，让我们去做吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes it is like, you need to do this, and sometimes it is like, we should talk about doing this, and sometimes it is, this is just kind of an FYI, we're thinking about it.
zh: 有时候就像这样，你需要做这个，有时候就像这样，我们应该谈谈做这个，有时候就像这样，这只是一个仅供参考，我们在考虑这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because it got big, we came up with that rubric of, we needed to tag each email with, do you want me to get this done this week, or is this something we should talk about, or is this something that's just FYI, I'm thinking about?
zh: 因为公司变大了，我们想出了这个标准，我们需要在每封邮件上打上标签，你是想让我这周做完这个，还是这是我们应该谈论的事情，还是这只是一个仅供参考，我在思考的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that... One of them is plea.
zh: 我喜欢那个……其中之一是 plea。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pleading you to do it.
zh: 恳求你去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not telling you to do this, I'm just pleading that you do what I ask.
zh: 我不是在告诉你要做这件事，我只是在恳求你按照我的要求去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh man.
zh: 天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This all connects.
zh: 这一切都是相连的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, you guys were co-founders for 20 years, you shared something before we started recording.
zh: 顺便说一下，你们是 20 年的联合创始人，你在我们开始录制之前分享了一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, Dharmesh famously did not ever want direct reports, he's just like, Brian, I want to start this with you, but I don't want to ever manage anyone.
zh: Dharmesh 出名地不想要任何直接下属，他就像那样，Brian，我想和你一起开始这个，但我永远不想管理任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you were talking about how you had to take on engineering, which didn't make any sense.
zh: 你在谈到你是如何不得不接手工程时，这根本没有任何意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I'm an engineer and I can code, but it's not good.
zh: 不，我是个工程师，我可以写代码，但写得不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, when we started the company he's like, "I was a CEO before, I was terrible at it, I don't want to do it again, you're going to be the CEO."
zh: 所以，当我们创办公司时，他说，“我以前是 CEO，我当得很糟糕，我不想再做了，你将是 CEO。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "Great."
zh: 我说，“太好了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, "And by the way, I'm not going to have any direct reports."
zh: 他说，“顺便说一句，我不想要任何直接下属。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "Well, it's just the two of us so don't have worry about it."
zh: 我说，“好吧，现在只有我们两个人，所以不用担心。”

speaker: Unknown
en: He's like, "No, ever, never."
zh: 他说，“不，永远，绝不。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "Yeah, yeah, yeah."
zh: 我说，“是啊，是啊，是啊。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we get 10, 12 people, we're starting to hire engineers, and onboard them, and making up big decisions, and I would go to him and be like, "Well, can you manage him?"
zh: 然后我们招到了 10、12 个人，我们开始招聘工程师，给他们入职培训，做出重大决定，我会去找他，说，“嗯，你能管理他吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: He is like, "Don't you remember I told you I don't want to have any direct reports?"
zh: 他说，“你不记得我告诉过你我不想有任何直接下属吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "Surely you were kidding when you said that?"
zh: 这就像是说，“当你说那话时，你肯定是在开玩笑吧？”

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, "Nope."
zh: 他说，“不。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, Dharmesh Shah has never had a single direct report at HubSpot.
zh: 所以，Dharmesh Shah 在 HubSpot 从来没有过一位直接下属。

speaker: Unknown
en: Incredible.
zh: 难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't, it's just like a dream, a way to operate, I love that you made it possible for him, and it created all this opportunity for him to tinker and innovate.
zh: 我不，这就像一场梦，一种运作方式，我很感激你为他实现了这一点，这为他创造了很多捣鼓和创新的机会。

speaker: Brian Halligan
en: Yes, yes, it freed him up to really think and be creative.
zh: 是的，是的，这解放了他，让他能够真正地去思考和发挥创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited to get him back on the podcast someday, we're going to link to that episode.
zh: 我很期待有一天能让他再次回到播客中，我们会链接到那一期节目。
